findings.evidence: Statements: `(hx : o.orientationAt x = positiveOrientation) : o.localOrientationOfZeroDim x = localOrientationOfZeroDimChart (chartAt E x) …`. The Mathlib convention is to name a theorem by its conclusion and spell out hypotheses after `of` (`C_of_A`).
findings.fix: Rename to `localOrientationOfZeroDim_eq_localOrientationOfZeroDimChart_of_orientationAt_eq` and `localOrientationOfZeroDim_eq_neg_localOrientationOfZeroDimChart_of_orientationAt_eq_neg`, and update the uses in `_neg` and `_eq_iff`.
findings.issue: `localOrientationOfZeroDim_of_eq` and `localOrientationOfZeroDim_of_eq_neg` (line 102) leave out the conclusion (equality with `localOrientationOfZeroDimChart`, or its negation) and give the hypothesis only as a bare `eq`/`eq_neg` instead of `orientationAt x = positiveOrientation`.

findings.evidence: Conclusion: `localHomologyRestriction … 0 (if o.orientationAt x = positiveOrientation then localHomologyPointClass … S x 1 else -(…)) = (o.localOrientationOfZeroDim x).val`.
findings.fix: Rename to `localHomologyRestriction_ite_localHomologyPointClass`, or restate the left-hand side so that `localOrientationOfZeroDim` is the restriction's argument.
findings.issue: The name `localHomologyRestriction_localOrientationOfZeroDim` reads as restriction applied to `localOrientationOfZeroDim`. In fact the restriction is applied to `ite … (localHomologyPointClass … S x 1)`, and `localOrientationOfZeroDim` appears only on the right-hand side.

summary: Namespaces and most new names follow existing conventions and no notation is added, but two theorem names do not describe their conclusions: the `_of_eq`/`_of_eq_neg` pair and `localHomologyRestriction_localOrientationOfZeroDim`.
